stories.title: Game of Drones: Deep strikes into Russia keeping Ukraine 'in this game'
stories.summary: Mark Owen is pleased to welcome Peter Zalmayev, Director of the Eurasia Democracy Initiative. He argues that Ukraine’s expanding long-range strike campaign has helped Ukraine “stay in this game” by raising the economic, military and social costs of Russia’s invasion and, crucially, by bringing the consequences of a distant war increasingly into Russian life. As Ukraine braces for another brutal winter with dangerously depleted air defenses, Kiev seeks to protect its own cities, civilians, and infrastructure.

stories.title: Japan to survey animal cafes over hygiene, welfare concerns
stories.summary: Japan will begin a survey in September to check hygiene and animal welfare at popular animal cafes. The survey will assess compliance with laws on animal space and cleanliness, with possible on-site inspections. Animal groups warn these cafes cause stress to animals and may involve endangered species and poor hygiene practices. Japan plans to probe popular animal cafes, where visitors can interact with anything from cats to capybaras, following concerns about hygiene and the creatures’ welfare, authorities said on Aug 27. Japan has hundreds of such cafes where campaigners say animals are sometimes kept in cramped spaces, and that their popularity encourages the capture and illegal trade of rare wildlife. A fact-finding survey will begin as early as September, starting with obtaining basic facts such like the number of establishments and what animals they keep, an environment ministry official told AFP. The ministry will examine whether they comply with relevant laws, including whether animals have enough space and how often cleaning takes place, said the official, without wishing to be named. “We may then do on-site inspections if we find facilities that appear to be breaching rules stipulated by the animal welfare law,” he said. The decision to launch the survey followed recommendations by members of an expert panel about animal welfare. Animal welfare groups have long been alarmed by the cafes, where visitors can pet and play with a dizzying array of animals including micro-pigs, hedgehogs, owls and snakes. They also included species covered by the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species, which regulates international trade in wildlife. Some shops had inadequate hygiene management without nudging users to handwash after contact with animals, and its “microbiological testing detected pathogenic bacteria in multiple facilities”, the report said.

stories.title: Kiev tries to convince West of military successes in absence of real results — Gerasimov
stories.summary: As part of a propaganda campaign, the Kiev regime is spreading false information about an allegedly successful offensive in the Zaporozhye Region
article_sentences: The Kiev regime is trying to convince the West of its battlefield successes despite the lack of real results, Russian Armed Forces’ General Staff Chief Army General Valery Gerasimov stated.
"In the absence of tangible results on the ground, the Ukrainian leadership is trying to convince its Western backers of the success of the Ukrainian military on the battlefield.
Therefore, as part of a propaganda campaign, it is spreading false information about an allegedly successful offensive in the Zaporozhye Region," he said.
